question: does the model ever call two tools in one response
supported_answer: Yes. Parallel tool use is the default: disable_parallel_tool_use defaults to false, and setting it to true is what restricts the model to a single tool use. Under tool_choice auto that cap is 'at most one tool use'; under any/tool it is 'exactly one'.

evidence.quote:
- `disable_parallel_tool_use: optional boolean`

      Whether to disable parallel tool use.

      Defaults to `false`. If set to `true`, the model will output at most one tool use.

atomic_claims: setting disable_parallel_tool_use to true makes the model output at most one tool use under tool_choice auto
reasoning_type: default-value inference from a parameter description
ambiguity_notes: The question does not name a provider. Answered from Anthropic because the asked-about behaviour is documented there; an OpenAI-scoped reading would need separate evidence.
verifier_notes: This exact block repeats at several offsets in the Messages document (35447, 128521, 482189, 624212...). The first canonical occurrence is anchored. Note the corpus distinguishes 'at most one' (auto) from 'exactly one' (any/tool) 130 chars later - the answer states both rather than flattening them. Span extended backwards from 35447 to the parameter declaration at 35392 after the integrity check found the snake_case identifier absent: the original span carried only the prose 'parallel tool use'.

question: what happens if my json schema has additionalProperties true with strict mode on
supported_answer: additionalProperties must be set to false for objects. The corpus states the constraint as a requirement of supported JSON Schema for both JSON outputs and strict tool use, so a schema setting it true is outside what structured outputs supports.

evidence.quote:
### JSON Schema limitations

Structured outputs support standard JSON Schema with some limitations. Both JSON outputs and strict tool use share these limitations.

<Accordion title="Supported features">
  * All basic types: object, array, string, integer, number, boolean, null
  * `enum` (strings, numbers, bools, or nulls only - no complex types; see [Invalid outputs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs#invalid-outputs) for a capitalization caveat)
  * `const`
  * `anyOf` and `allOf` (with limitations - `allOf` with `$ref` not supported)
  * `$ref`, `$def`, and `definitions` (external `$ref` not supported)
  * `default` property for all supported types
  * `required` and `additionalProperties` (must be set to `false` for objects

atomic_claims: structured outputs support standard JSON Schema with limitations
the limitations apply to both JSON outputs and strict tool use
additionalProperties must be set to false for objects

question: screenshot resolution for computer use — does it matter what size my screen is
supported_answer: Yes. Returned coordinates are relative and must be rescaled to whatever surface you act on; padding is applied only to the bottom and right edges so the origin does not shift and a per-axis linear rescale suffices. On HiDPI displays, where screenshot pixels differ from logical coordinates, you must additionally divide by the display scale factor.

evidence.quote:
Padding is applied only to the bottom and right edges, so the origin doesn't shift and a per-axis linear rescale is sufficient. Clamp returned coordinates to the resized dimensions before rescaling, so a point slightly outside the image can't map outside your original.

The relative coordinates multiply against whatever surface you act on: the original image, a full-resolution scan, or a screen. When you act on a screen and screenshot pixels differ from logical coordinates (HiDPI displays), also divide by the display scale factor. The [Computer use tool's scaling guidance](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#handle-coordinate-scaling-for-higher-resolutions) covers that patte

on HiDPI displays you must also divide by the display scale factor
